title: torch.compile mode="max-autotune" precision appears to be lower
body: I'm training a model compiled with torch.compile. With otherwise identical runs, the loss curve using mode="max-autotune" is noticeably less stable than the default-mode curve, while max-autotune is slightly faster. The forward pass is wrapped in torch.autocast, and I see no graph breaks or warnings. This was initially observed on an RTX A6000 with PyTorch 2.1.0.dev20230307; the submitted environment dump was collected on a system listing an RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU. I do not yet have a minified reproduction and can test specific settings if given guidance.

symptoms_visible: My max-autotune training run has a noticeably noisier and less stable loss curve than the otherwise identical default-mode run.
The max-autotune run is slightly faster, and I do not see graph breaks or warning messages.
N0.label: N0 unstable max-autotune training reported

symptoms_visible: On the 2023-07-06 development build, run_repro reports an accuracy problem for the extracted graph, although the minifier cannot simplify it further.
N1.label: N1 accuracy failure reproduced in extracted graph

symptoms_visible: Turning TF32 off does not make the max-autotune model converge.
The default max-autotune combination does not converge; max-autotune GEMM with pointwise autotuning disabled converges noisily; runs without the problematic CUDA-graph combination are smooth.
Repeated runs with the same configuration produce nearly overlapping loss curves.
N2.label: N2 stable configuration-dependent behavior established

symptoms_visible: After replacing the wall-clock scheduler with a fixed equivalent schedule and removing the batch-size ramp, I can still trigger fast runs with bad accuracy when determinism is disabled.
Enabling deterministic algorithms makes the run slow and produces repeated CUDA-graph warnings, while disabling determinism makes it fast and inaccurate without that warning.
The same inaccurate behavior occurs with caches force-disabled.
N3.label: N3 scheduler and cache confounders controlled

symptoms_visible: On PyTorch 2.6.0.dev20240915, reduce-overhead with deterministic algorithms disabled still produces the bad loss curve.
With determinism enabled the run is very slow and repeatedly fails to use CUDA graphs; without CUDA graphs the compiled run has no major accuracy issue.
N4.label: N4 issue persists on PyTorch 2.6 development build

symptoms_visible: In my minimal four-step gradient-accumulation reproduction, the eager baseline produces the expected accumulated gradient, while affected compiled CUDA-graph configurations produce different gradients.
On PyTorch 2.10, the CUDA-graph-trees configuration raises an error instead of silently returning the bad accumulated result, while the non-tree CUDA-graph path still accumulates inaccurately.
N5.label: N5 gradient-accumulation interaction isolated

symptoms_visible: My PyTorch 2.10 minimal reproduction is stopped by a correctness error on the CUDA-graph-trees path rather than silently completing with the wrong accumulated gradient; I have not reported a successful corrected training run.
N_terminal.label: terminal closed with correctness guard but no successful training confirmation

question_patterns: Can you provide a smaller script or extracted graph that still reports the accuracy problem?
Could you rerun the accuracy checker on a recent nightly and share its raw result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found a compact extracted graph on torch 2.1.0.dev20230706. run_repro correctly reports an accuracy problem, but the minifier cannot simplify the graph any further, so I have pasted the generated reproduction.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The extracted graph passes the accuracy checker in every compile mode; I can only see a difference in the full training application.
run_repro reports the same accuracy failure on a nightly from a few days later.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c6 on the reporter's own GPU and PyTorch 2.1.0.dev20230706 environment. The answer reports only run_repro's output and the failed minification, not a cause.

question_patterns: Can you rerun with both CUDA matmul and cuDNN TF32 disabled and report whether the model converges?
Does disabling allow_tf32 change the bad loss curve?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I turned off both allow_tf32 settings. It does not fix max-autotune precision, and the model still does not converge.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With both TF32 settings disabled, max-autotune converges and its loss curve matches the default run.

question_patterns: Can you compare the training curves across the individual compile-setting combinations?
Please run the remaining configuration combinations and report which ones converge or become noisy.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The default max-autotune combination with GEMM autotuning, pointwise autotuning and CUDA graphs does not converge. GEMM autotuning with pointwise autotuning disabled and CUDA graphs enabled converges but is noisy. The other combinations, including the run without CUDA graphs and default mode with either autotuning knob enabled individually, are smooth.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every configuration, including the one without CUDA graphs, fails with the same non-converging loss curve.
The same combinations separate into smooth, noisy and non-converging runs, but throughput differs by less than one percent.

edges.comment: Reporter measurements from c11-c16 and c22. These are configuration probes, so they remain clarification-only. The reporter later stated repeated runs nearly overlap; that unprompted stability observation is introduced in N2.volunteered_info.

question_patterns: Can you replace the wall-clock-dependent schedule and remove other changing inputs, then rerun the comparison?
Please control the learning-rate schedule and batch-size ramp so the runs receive equivalent training inputs.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I replaced the budget schedule with a fixed but equivalent triangular schedule and turned off the batch-size ramp. That removes the slow, schedule-lagging failure mode, but I can still produce fast runs with bad accuracy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After replacing the timed scheduler and batch ramp, all configurations have identical per-step losses and the accuracy problem disappears.

question_patterns: With the other sources of nondeterminism controlled, how do the runs behave when deterministic algorithms are enabled versus disabled?
Can you compare throughput, warnings and loss with the determinism setting in both states?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With deterministic algorithms disabled, reduce-overhead reliably runs fast, prints no CUDA-graph warning, and gives the bad accuracy. With deterministic algorithms enabled, the warning appears and the run is slow but correct.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The loss remains wrong with deterministic algorithms enabled and disabled, and both runs have the same speed and warnings.
The same accuracy split occurs, but the deterministic run is only moderately slower.

question_patterns: Can you force compilation caches off and report whether the inaccurate run changes?
Does rerunning with cache-disabling settings remove the problem?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. The fast inaccurate behavior happens with and without TORCHINDUCTOR_FORCE_DISABLE_CACHES=1, and disabling the local autotune cache does not fix it either.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Forcing caches off completely removes the accuracy problem, and it returns as soon as I reuse the cached artifacts.

edges.comment: Reporter-controlled reruns from c30-c36 on the reporter's training setup. The timed scheduler was a real confounder in some runs but did not explain the fast inaccurate runs. Cache toggles are measurements, not solution attempts.

question_patterns: Does the controlled training comparison still reproduce on a more recent PyTorch nightly?
Please rerun the relevant configurations on a current development build and share the resulting curves.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reran the tests on PyTorch 2.6.0.dev20240915. The precision issue remains for reduce-overhead with deterministic algorithms disabled. Turning determinism on is very slow because the code repeatedly tries and fails to run CUDA graphs, while the compiled run without CUDA graphs has no major issue. Here is the new plot.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: On the recent nightly, every configuration now follows the same loss curve and the earlier problem no longer reproduces.
The same configuration still has the bad curve on a nearby 2.6 development nightly.

edges.comment: Reporter retest from c39-c44 on the reporter's own setup. The c44 attachment is attached here because it directly answers the request for current-build curves.

question_patterns: Can you reduce the current problem to a standalone numerical reproduction and compare the relevant execution configurations?
Please share a minimal script and its raw eager-versus-compiled gradient results on a current PyTorch build.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reduced it to a small MLP that performs four backward calls for gradient accumulation and compares each parameter gradient with eager. The eager fc3.bias gradient is 1.0 as expected. The affected compiled CUDA-graph configurations produce different accumulated gradients. On PyTorch 2.10, the trees configuration raises a correctness error instead of silently returning the bad result, while the non-tree CUDA-graph path still accumulates inaccurately.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The standalone test produces the same gradients in eager and every compiled configuration, including across all four accumulation steps.
The same standalone test reproduces with a different hidden size and batch size.

question_patterns: What happens in the current build when the standalone reproduction exercises each compiled configuration?
Does the current build silently return a differing gradient, raise an error, or match eager?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the trees configuration on PyTorch 2.10, I now get a crash or correctness error rather than a silently inaccurate accumulated gradient.

question_patterns: What does the other compiled configuration return in the same current-build test?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The non-tree CUDA-graph configuration still completes with inaccurate gradient accumulation in my PyTorch 2.10 test.

edges.comment: Reporter analysis and minimal reproduction from c45 on the reporter's PyTorch 2.10 environment. The reporter independently states that the issue is the CUDA-graph-trees and gradient-accumulation interaction; that unprompted conclusion enters N5.volunteered_info rather than being smuggled into the questions.

solution.intent: Treat the original loss degradation as silent incorrect gradient accumulation in the older CUDA-graph execution path, not reduced floating-point precision. Use the current CUDA-graph-trees default and its correctness check so the unsupported case fails loudly instead of silently training with wrong gradients; avoid the inaccurate non-tree CUDA-graph path, and ask the reporter to verify a corrected training configuration before claiming full resolution.
solution.concrete_example: The minimal reproduction isolates incorrect gradient accumulation when compiled CUDA-graph execution is used. Current CUDA-graph trees detect the unsafe case and raise an error rather than silently accumulating the wrong gradients. Keep the checked trees path as the default, or disable CUDA graphs for this workload, and rerun the real training job before considering the numerical problem resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the minimal gradient outputs and identified the trees-plus-gradient-accumulation interaction. The maintainer's final interpretation is that the current default trees path and its existing correctness check adequately guard this class of silent error. That guard prevents silent corruption but does not establish that the reporter completed a correct full training run.

edges.comment: Maintainer closure from c46-c47 after the reporter's c45 PyTorch 2.10 reproduction. The maintainer says CUDA-graph trees have long been default and the correctness check catches these errors. The reporter did not reply to confirm a successful corrected training run, so the terminal remains unresolved from the user's perspective.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted diagnosis: the apparent max-autotune precision loss came from incorrect gradient accumulation associated with CUDA-graph execution, specifically the CUDA-graph-trees interaction in older behavior, rather than ordinary floating-point precision loss.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the controlled configuration runs and the standalone gradient-accumulation reproduction, including the differing eager and compiled gradients.

Must not settle on TF32, persistent compilation caches, or the wall-clock learning-rate scheduler as the root cause: TF32 and cache disabling did not fix the failure, and the fast inaccurate behavior remained after scheduler and batch-ramp controls.

Must distinguish the current correctness guard from a numerical fix: the trees path now raises an error instead of silently returning wrong accumulated gradients, while the reporter still observed inaccurate accumulation on the non-tree CUDA-graph path.

Must avoid recommending the known inaccurate non-tree CUDA-graph path for this gradient-accumulation workload; using the checked trees path or disabling CUDA graphs is the safe direction established by the thread.

Must ask the reporter to verify the real training workload with a safe configuration before declaring the issue fully resolved; the thread closed without the reporter confirming a successful corrected training run.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical machine-learning practitioner who can run long controlled training experiments, modify TorchInductor settings, inspect warnings and throughput, prepare generated and minimal reproductions, and compare parameter gradients and storage pointers.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative, analytical and candid about uncertainty; supplies detailed plots, scripts and configuration matrices, corrects earlier hypotheses as new evidence arrives, and may need substantial time to complete full training reruns.
